The second assertion is a little more difficult to prove, but
it is a consequence of the assertion that the $G_{V}$ -action on
$\mu^{-1}(0)_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}^{\mathrm{s}}$ is free and closed. For our
applications, this will be important as Poincaré duality isomorphism
holds for $\mu^{-1}(0)_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}^{\mathrm{s}}/G_{V}$ .

It is known that the $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -semistability automatically implies
the $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stability unless $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ lies in a finite union of
hyperplanes in ${\mathbb{R}}^{Q_{0}}$ . In this case, it is known that the natural
map

(3.1)

$\pi\colon\mu^{-1}(0)_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}^{\mathrm{s}}/G_{V}\to\mu^{-1}(0)/\!\!/G_{V}$

is proper, i.e., inverse images of compact subsets remain
compact. Here the map is defined by assigning $\sim$ -equivalence
classes to $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stable $G_{V}$ -orbits. If $(B,I,J)$ is regarded
as a framed representation of the preprojective algebra, it is sent to
its ‘semisimplification’ under $\pi$ .

When $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ lies in a finite union of hyperplanes, $\pi$ is not
proper. We need to replace $\mu^{-1}(0)_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}^{\mathrm{s}}/G_{V}$
by a larger space, a certain quotient of the space of
$\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -semistable points in $\mu^{-1}(0)$ , similar to
$\mu^{-1}(0)/\!\!/G_{V}$ .
We do not consider such $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ . We always assume
$\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stability and $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -semistability are equivalent
hereafter.

Let us denote $\mu^{-1}(0)_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}^{\mathrm{s}}/G_{V}$ by
${\mathfrak{M}}_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}(V,W)$ . We will use the case $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}_{i}>0$ for all
$i\in Q_{0}$ later. In this case we simply denote it by ${\mathfrak{M}}(V,W)$ . The
inverse image $\pi^{-1}(0)$ will be important. Let us denote it by
${\mathfrak{L}}(V,W)$ .

For a $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}$ -stable framed representation $(B,I,J)$ , the
corresponding point in ${\mathfrak{M}}_{\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}}(V,W)$ is denoted by $[B,I,J]$ .

paper.title: Introduction to quiver varieties -- for ring and representation theoriests
paper.abstract: We review the definition of quiver varieties and their relation to representation theory of Kac-Moody Lie algebras. Target readers are ring and representation theorists. We emphasize important roles of first extension groups of the preprojective algebra associated with a quiver.
